title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: App Blocks turn requests into interactive apps in the conversation
summary: Hold: the data-exposure guidance incorrectly presents explicitly supplied prompt content as the only way Copilot Chat uses organisational content. Microsoft also documents open content in Teams and Outlook and pay-as-you-go agents; the cited blocking instructions additionally disagree about user scoping and Teams coverage.

Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps.
Select the Available Apps list.
Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane.
Select Block app.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Manage Copilot Chat says the block can be scoped to specific users or groups, including licensed users.
claims.quote: Blocking Copilot through Integrated Apps is a tenant-wide control that you can scope to specific users or groups, including licensed users.
claims.fix: After the scoping sentence add: 'However, the cited Integrated Apps instructions say that choosing Block app blocks all users in the organisation; confirm the effective scope before relying on a selective block.' The conflicting source is https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/teams-apps-work-on-outlook-and-m365#how-to-block-an-app.

claims.claim: Manage Copilot Chat says Integrated Apps blocking covers the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook and Copilot Chat on the web.
claims.quote: This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.
claims.fix: Attribute the coverage sentence to Manage Copilot Chat and add: 'The Integrated Apps page instead says the app is blocked only in Microsoft Copilot and Outlook, while Teams continues to honour its Teams admin center setting.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/teams-apps-work-on-outlook-and-m365#how-to-block-an-app for the disagreement.
